name: Question 8
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14054607/assets/933e68e42fe61af3e30fae012b0b56dce6793b0fadc343e04a0766b85cb6ae7e.png)

If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $y=9-{x}^{2}$ and $y=1+{x}^{2},$ as shown above, then ${∬}_{D}(x{y}^{2}+2x)\,dA=$
worked_solution:
First, let's represent $D$ as a type I region. 

- To determine the $x$-limits, we need to find the $x$-coordinates of the points at which the curves intersect. So, we set the following equation and solve it for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1+{x}^{2} & =9-{x}^{2} \\ 2{x}^{2} & =8 \\ {x}^{2} & =4 \\ x & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x$-limits are 
$-2\le x\le 2.$

- To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14054607/assets/c56c5be4ac88755f1859f295f700be8710d75b16380ac120e6b56a3aa767acbe.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 2,\,1+{x}^{2}\le y\le 9-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}(x{y}^{2}+2x)\,dA & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{1+{x}^{2}}^{9-{x}^{2}}(x{y}^{2}+2x)\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

If D is the finite region enclosed by the curves y=9−x2 and y=1+x2, as shown above, then ∬D(xy2+2x)dA=

a
∫−22∫1+x29−x2(xy2+2x)dydx
b
∫−29−x2∫29−x2(xy2+2x)dydx
c
∫−20∫02(xy2+2x)dydx
d
∫1+x22∫9−x22(xy2+2x)dydx
e
∫1+x29−x2∫−22(xy2+2x)dydx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's represent D as a type I region.

  • To determine the x-limits, we need to find the x-coordinates of the points at which the curves intersect. So, we set the following equation and solve it for x: 1+x2=9−x22x2=8x2=4x=±2 So, x-limits are −2≤x≤2.

  • To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

As a result, we get

D={(x,y):−2≤x≤2,1+x2≤y≤9−x2}.

Therefore, we can express the integral as follows:

∬D(xy2+2x)dA=∫−22∫1+x29−x2(xy2+2x)dydx
